name: Safaricom
summary: Kenya's largest telco and home of M-PESA. Little is published about engineering interviews, so treat this outline as indicative only.

process.note: Safaricom does not publish a standard engineering interview loop. Every stage below is based on candidate reports and may differ by role.

stages.name: Application
stages.detail: Candidates typically apply online through the careers portal and are screened against the role.

stages.name: Online assessment
stages.detail: Some candidates report a timed online test, which may include coding or aptitude questions.

stages.name: Panel interview
stages.detail: Often described as a panel mixing technical questions with competency questions.

stages.name: Technical exercise
stages.detail: Some roles are reported to include a case study or practical exercise.

stages.name: Final interview
stages.detail: A final or HR conversation is commonly reported before an offer and checks.

design.note: Little is published. Mobile money and messaging at national scale make payments and reliable notification useful practice.

values.title: The Spirit of Safaricom
values.summary: Safaricom's published reports describe the Spirit of Safaricom through a few pillars. The names are Safaricom's; the readings are ours.

items.name: Purpose
items.gist: Connect your work to transforming lives and to the people who rely on the service.

items.name: Customer obsession
items.gist: Understand customers deeply and design around what they actually need.

items.name: Collaboration
items.gist: Work across teams and partners to deliver more than any one group could.

items.name: Innovation
items.gist: Look for new ways to solve problems and be willing to try them.

prompts.text: Describe work you did that made a real difference to the people using it. How did you know?
Tell a story where understanding a customer better changed what you built.
Talk about a project that needed several teams or partners. How did you keep it moving?
Share a time you tried a new approach to an old problem. What did you learn?

mock.note: A cautious guess based on candidate reports: a coding round, a design or case exercise and a competency conversation.
